Definition: without profit, worthlessness; by extension, destruction, wickedness
BiblicalUsage: The word beliyaal means worthlessness, wickedness, and it appears 26 times across the Bible. Hannah was mistaken for a daughter of Belial, the men of Gibeah were sons of Belial, and Shimei cursed David as a man of Belial.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe worthlessness is not a small sin; a person who is good for nothing to God has chosen ruin, and only grace makes anyone profitable again. That is why I keep coming back to it: beliyaal is not a word to rush past.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
